title: Implement and Integrate a New 'Diffusion' Training Strategy
description: CineWave Maestro, an adaptive music score generation platform, needs to be updated with a more modern training technique to improve the quality and novelty of its generated audio. The existing `training_worker` service is designed with a Strategy pattern, allowing different training algorithms (like the current GAN-based one) to be used interchangeably. This multi-session task involves implementing the scaffolding for a new 'Diffusion' model strategy, integrating it into the system's factory, and making it configurable.

project_spec.name: CineWave Maestro: Adaptive Score Training Platform
project_spec.description:
CineWave Maestro is a hard-level, C-centric MLOps platform that trains, serves and continuously improves machine-learning models which compose and remix background music and sound-effects for films, games and live-streamed events in real time. Each microservice owns a discrete responsibility—data ingestion from licensed sound libraries, feature extraction on audio wave-forms, model training for genre-specific style transfer, and low-latency model serving to downstream game engines or editing suites—so studios can experiment rapidly with new audio styles without halting production.

Built around Strategy, Observer, Factory and Pipeline patterns, CineWave Maestro lets sound engineers push new "sound strategies" (model variants) into an experiment-tracking service, automatically versioned in the feature store. Hyperparameter-tuning workers spin up containers that compile native C kernels (e.g., FFT, mel-spectrogram, differentiable DSP filters) and call the TensorFlow C API for accelerated training. Upon reaching evaluation thresholds, models are promoted via a model registry; observers trigger redeployment to live soundtracks on streaming platforms. Continuous monitoring detects audio drift (e.g., audience sentiment or loudness mismatches) and invokes automated retraining pipelines, keeping the entertainment experience fresh and on-brand.
dependencies: ZeroMQ (low-latency intra-cluster messaging for audio chunks)
Redis (feature value cache & pub/sub for hot-reloads)
Docker + Kubernetes (container orchestration, automated retraining jobs)
CppUTest / CMocka (unit & integration tests from the C side)
